Supported UI Language Catalog
nodes.rationale: Every locale file carries the full 44-language menu translated into its own language, plus a withSystem option, so users can switch away from a language they cannot read without needing to find English first.

nodes.label: Admin vs Viewer Role Model
nodes.rationale: Two-tier UI role split: admins get full UI access, viewers are deliberately limited to watching cameras, review items and historical footage so read-only accounts cannot mutate config or delete media.

nodes.label: Config Override Control Vocabulary
nodes.rationale: Shared modified/overridden/resetToGlobal/resetToDefault labels give the settings UI a single vocabulary for three-state values (default, global, per-camera override) instead of per-section wording.

nodes.label: Frigate Chat Assistant
nodes.rationale: Tool-calling LLM assistant over cameras and events: it surfaces which tools were called with their arguments and results, exposes reasoning/thinking traces, reports tokens and tokens-per-second, and lets an event be attached by id so answers are grounded in a specific tracked object.

nodes.label: Safe Mode Config Editor
nodes.rationale: When config validation fails Frigate boots into safe mode and the editor is the only surface left, so it is labelled distinctly and offers save-only alongside save-and-restart to avoid a restart loop on a still-broken config.

nodes.label: Effective Retain Mode
nodes.rationale: Manual on-demand recording cannot save more than the configured record retain mode allows, so the UI resolves the effective mode (all / motion / active_objects) and warns that only matching segments are kept, or that only a snapshot is saved when recording is disabled.

nodes.label: Face Recognition Training Loop
nodes.rationale: Recognition needs at least one face in the library to work at all, so the flow is upload a frontal image, then use the Train tab on recent recognition attempts to reinforce each collection. Angled training images are called out as harmful to accuracy. Sub-label score is a weighted score across all recognized-face confidences, so it can differ from the score shown on the snapshot.

nodes.label: Catalan Settings View Translations
nodes.rationale: Largest locale namespace (~114KB). Holds documentTitle/menu/dialog trees for every settings sub-page (cameras, masks and zones, motion tuner, users, roles, notifications, enrichments, triggers, global config, system config). The flat menu.system* key family mirrors the System view's sub-pages, so settings acts as the navigation shell over system configuration.

nodes.label: Catalan System View Translations
nodes.rationale: Namespaces system metrics UI: general (detector, hardwareInfo, otherProcesses), storage (recordings, cameraStorage, shm), cameras (framesAndDetections, connectionQuality), enrichments (embeddings, infPerSecond) and a stats.* family of health warnings (shmTooLow, detectIsSlow, ffmpegHighCpuUsage, cameraIsOffline) that maps one-to-one onto backend stats thresholds.

nodes.label: Debug Replay Session
nodes.rationale: Creates a temporary replay camera that loops historical footage with the source camera's detect settings so object detection and tracking issues can be reproduced. Tuning changes made during a session are explicitly not written to the Frigate config file, and stopping the session clears temporary data; only one session may be active at a time.

nodes.label: Export Case Grouping
nodes.rationale: Exports are grouped into named cases with a description; multi-camera and multi-review batch exports all land in a single case so an incident stays together. Uncategorized exports remain a first-class bucket, and deleting a case can either keep or permanently delete its exports.

nodes.label: Export Job Lifecycle
nodes.rationale: An export job moves through queued, running, preparing, copying, encoding, encoding retry and finalizing states, exposed so long remuxes do not look hung.

nodes.label: Classification Model Creation Wizard
nodes.rationale: Two model kinds with different semantics: state models watch a fixed camera area for changes (door open/closed, minimum 2 classes) while object models classify detected objects. Object classifications land either as sub-labels (appended text on the object label) or as attributes (searchable metadata stored separately). Sample images are pulled from recordings so users can train without hand-collecting a dataset.

nodes.label: Retraining Requirement on Dataset Change
nodes.rationale: Deleting a class, renaming a class or deleting dataset images all invalidate the trained weights, so the UI warns that the model must be retrained (and state class changes need a model restart to take effect).

nodes.label: Motion Search ROI Scan
nodes.rationale: Pixel-change scan over recordings inside a user-drawn polygon. Knobs are all speed/completeness trade-offs: parallel mode scans multiple recording segments at once but uses more decode resources, frameSkip processes every Nth frame (set to camera FPS for one frame per second) and is faster but can miss short motion events, maxResults stops early. Segments are skipped when inactive or when they do not overlap the ROI heatmap, with a full-range fallback.

nodes.label: Annotation Offset
nodes.rationale: Bounding boxes come from the detect stream but are drawn over record-stream footage, and the two streams are never perfectly synchronized, so annotation_offset shifts annotations forward or backward in milliseconds; the value may be negative and is tuned by watching whether boxes lead or lag a walking person.

nodes.label: Tracked Object Lifecycle
nodes.rationale: A tracked object is described by a fixed set of lifecycle events (visible, active, stationary, entered_zone, attribute, heard, external, gone) that the timeline renders in order.

nodes.label: Tracking Details Panel
nodes.rationale: A second, newer rendering of the same lifecycle event vocabulary that adds score, computedScore, topScore headers and an advanced-scores toggle for debugging detection confidence.

nodes.label: Global vs Per-Camera Section Split
nodes.rationale: Each config section (audio, motion, detect, objects, record, snapshots, timestamp_style) declares parallel global and cameras headings so the same Pydantic schema renders once as a system default and once as a per-camera override, with ffmpeg camera-only because global ffmpeg args are not per-camera overridable in the same way.

nodes.label: Detector Backend Catalog
nodes.rationale: One config node enumerates every supported inference backend (cpu, deepstack, degirum, edgetpu, hailo8l, memryx, onnx, openvino, rknn, synaptics, teflon_tfl, tensorrt, zmq, axengine) so hardware choice is a config value rather than a build variant.

nodes.label: Semantic Search Configuration
nodes.rationale: Semantic search is gated on downloading vision and text embedding models and on a reindex pass, so it ships disabled and exposes model/model_size/device knobs to trade accuracy against limited NVR hardware.

nodes.label: Generative AI Provider Configuration
nodes.rationale: GenAI is configured as a pluggable provider (api_key, base_url, model, provider, roles, provider_options, runtime_options) so descriptions, review summaries and chat can be routed to local or hosted LLMs without code changes.

nodes.label: Authentication Configuration
nodes.rationale: Auth exposes failed_login_rate_limit, hash_iterations, session_length, trusted_proxies and admin_first_time_login so a locally hosted NVR can be hardened or fronted by a reverse proxy without an external identity provider.

nodes.label: Dashboard Stream Method Selection
nodes.rationale: Three modes trade bandwidth against latency: no streaming refreshes once a minute, smart streaming (recommended) refreshes once a minute until activity is detected then switches to live, continuous streaming is always live and is explicitly warned about for bandwidth and performance. The choice is stored per device/browser, not in the server config.

nodes.label: Stream Compatibility Mode
nodes.rationale: Opt-in workaround, enabled only when the live stream shows color artifacts and a diagonal line on the right edge of the image, rather than being applied to every camera by default.

nodes.label: Batch and Multi-Camera Export
nodes.rationale: Multi-camera export preselects cameras that actually have tracked objects in the chosen time range, and reports partial success per camera (successful/total plus failed camera names) because individual exports can fail independently.

nodes.label: Global vs Per-Camera Config Override Model
Czech Audio Label Translations
nodes.rationale: Flat map of AudioSet/YAMNet class ids (yell, speech, bark, footsteps, applause) to Czech display names. Keys are the raw audio model class labels, so this file is a display layer over the audio detection model's label set.

nodes.label: Czech Object Label Translations
nodes.rationale: Flat map of COCO detection labels (person, car, dog, license_plate-adjacent classes) plus Frigate's synthetic grouping labels (animal, vehicle) to Czech names. Keyed by the detector's raw label strings.

nodes.label: Czech Common Translations
nodes.rationale: Shared vocabulary for every view: time.* presets (last7, thisWeek, 12hours) and button.* actions. Uses Czech's three-form plural suffixes (_one/_few/_other) for year/month/day/hour/minute/second, which English locale files express with only _one/_other.

nodes.label: Czech Camera Config Translations (empty)
nodes.rationale: Empty object. Config namespaces are machine-generated from Pydantic field titles and descriptions by generate_config_translations.py, so non-English locales stay empty until translators fill them and must never be hand-edited.

nodes.label: Frigate+ model service and snapshot submission
Motion detection tuner (threshold, contour area, improve contrast)
Motion masks, object masks, and zones editor
Czech Config Editor View Translations
nodes.rationale: Small namespace but encodes the editor's two-path save model: saveAndRestart versus saveOnly, plus safeConfigEditor and safeModeDescription for the degraded startup path.

nodes.label: Czech Explore View Translations
nodes.rationale: Tracked-object detail surface: generativeAI descriptions with regenerateFromSnapshot / regenerateFromThumbnails, sub-label and license plate editing, estimatedSpeed, objectLifecycle carousel with createObjectMask and autoTracking tips, itemMenu actions (findSimilar, submitToPlus, addTrigger, audioTranscription), and exploreIsUnavailable states tied to embeddings reindexing and model downloads.

nodes.label: Czech Face Library View Translations
nodes.rationale: Face recognition dataset management: drag-and-drop image entry with size and pixel validation, createFaceLibrary onboarding steps, train/reprocess/rename/delete face flows, deleteFaceAttempts, and subLabelScore detail strings.

nodes.label: Czech Live View Translations
nodes.rationale: Live camera controls as paired enable/disable keys per capability (camera, detect, recording, snapshots, audioDetect, autotracking, twoWayTalk, cameraAudio, streamStats), PTZ controls (move, zoom, focus, presets), lowBandwidthMode, suspend.forTime, and a manualRecording state machine (start/started/failedToStart/end/ended/failedToEnd, recordDisabledTips).

nodes.label: Czech Classification Model View Translations
nodes.rationale: Strings for the custom classifier lifecycle: create/edit model, categorize images, rename and delete categories (guarded by minClasses), delete dataset and train images, and trainModel with tooltips gating on trainingInProgress / noNewImages / noChanges / modelNotReady.

nodes.label: Czech Events (Review) View Translations
nodes.rationale: Review-item vocabulary: alerts/detections/motion severity tabs, markAsReviewed, newReviewItems, empty states per severity plus recordingsDisabled, timeline and objectTrack (trackedPoint, clickToSeek) seek affordances, and activity classification labels (normalActivity, suspiciousActivity, threateningActivity, securityConcern, needsReview).

nodes.label: Czech Filter Component Translations
nodes.rationale: Single namespace backing every filter bar: labels, subLabels, zones, score, timeRange, dates presets, sort orders, features (hasSnapshot/hasVideoClip/submittedToFrigatePlus), recognizedLicensePlates, logSettings severity filtering, and zoneMask. Filter chips render object and zone names sourced from objects.json.

nodes.label: Czech Player Component Translations
nodes.rationale: Player-surface strings: empty states (noRecordingsFoundForThisTime, noPreviewFound, streamOffline, cameraDisabled), an iOS version gate, Frigate+ submission, and a stats.* family (streamType, bandwidth, latency, totalFrames, droppedFrames, decodedFrames, droppedFrameRate) that names the live stream telemetry fields.

nodes.label: Czech Camera Component Translations
nodes.rationale: Two concerns in one namespace: group.* (camera group CRUD, icon picker, showAll/showLess) and debug.* overlay toggles (zones, motion, regions, timestamp, boundingBox, mask, paths) that correspond to the debug view's per-frame annotation layers.

nodes.label: Czech Dialog Component Translations
nodes.rationale: Covers the modal surfaces shared across views: restart, export (including multiCamera and fromTimeline flows), streaming/restreaming stats, saveSearch, and the imagePicker. Export dialog strings are the producer side of the Exports view's consumer strings.

nodes.label: Crash-loop restart backoff
nodes.rationale: Restart timestamps are kept in a bounded deque and pruned against a sliding 60 second window; after 5 restarts inside that window the watchdog stops respawning and only logs. This stops a process that fails immediately on start from being restarted forever and burying the real error in log noise. Exit code 0 is treated as an intentional exit and logged once, never restarted.

nodes.label: Stuck detection recovery
nodes.rationale: A detector whose detection_start timestamp is more than 10 seconds old is presumed wedged (usually a hung hardware accelerator) and is restarted in place. If the detect process is outright dead, the whole of Frigate is restarted instead, because detection is not optional and a partially working NVR silently missing objects is worse than a visible restart.

nodes.label: Internal comms topic constants
nodes.rationale: Every inter-process ZMQ topic name is centralized as a constant so publisher and subscriber cannot drift apart on a string literal.

nodes.label: setup_logging (queue-based logging)
nodes.rationale: All processes push records onto a manager Queue consumed by a single QueueListener in the main process, so multiple processes never interleave writes on one stream handler. The root logger's own handlers are cleared with force=True so nothing bypasses the queue.

nodes.label: reopen_std_streams fork hook
nodes.rationale: Registered via os.register_at_fork(after_in_child) to work around CPython issue 91776: if a process is forked while a logging thread holds an internal stdio lock, the child inherits the held lock and deadlocks when Python flushes stdout/stderr at exit. Reopening fds 1 and 2 in the child gives it fresh, unlocked stream objects.

nodes.label: LogPipe (subprocess stderr capture)
nodes.rationale: Buffers the last 100 lines in a bounded deque and only emits them on dump(), so a noisy ffmpeg process does not flood the log until something actually fails. Every line passes through clean_camera_user_pass so RTSP credentials never reach the log.

nodes.label: suppress_stderr_during
nodes.rationale: Native libraries (LLVM, CUDA, TFLite) write straight to file descriptor 2 and ignore Python logging config entirely, so the only way to silence them is to dup2 /dev/null over fd 2 for the duration of the call and restore it afterward.

nodes.label: TimelineProcessor.insert_or_save (pre-event cache)
nodes.rationale: Timeline rows for an object with neither a clip nor a snapshot are buffered in pre_event_cache instead of inserted, because the parent Event row does not exist yet and the timeline would reference a missing event. Once the event is saved, the cached entries are flushed in order ahead of the current one.

nodes.label: TimelineProcessor.handle_object_detection
nodes.rationale: Boxes and regions are converted to relative coordinates against the detect resolution before storage so timeline data stays valid if the detect resolution later changes. One update can emit several rows (entered_zone, stationary/active, attribute), and entered_zone is suppressed for stationary objects and for transitions out of all zones.

nodes.label: Config validation error reporting and safe mode fallback
nodes.rationale: On a pydantic ValidationError the raw YAML is reloaded with ruamel round-trip parsing purely to walk the error loc path and recover line numbers, since pydantic errors carry no source position. Rather than exiting, Frigate retries FrigateConfig.load(safe_load=True) so the UI comes up in safe mode and the user can fix the config from the web interface instead of the filesystem.

nodes.label: Forkserver start method with module preload
nodes.rationale: Frigate forces the forkserver start method and preloads sqlite3, numpy, cv2, peewee, zmq, ruamel.yaml, and frigate.camera.maintainer into the server process. Forkserver avoids inheriting the parent's threads and locks (which fork would deadlock on), while preloading the heavy imports once amortizes import cost across every camera process spawned later.

nodes.label: iGPU Name Fallback to CPU Name
Full-scan fallback when all segments gated out
Single concurrent job per job type
VOD HLS input for SPS/PPS stitching
Search routing policy (label vs sub_label vs semantic_query)
Ollama non-streaming fallback for tool calls
get_standard_aspect_ratio
nodes.rationale: Only a fixed set of known aspect ratios is allowed, all scaled to a common relative size, so cameras of differing shapes tile into the birdseye canvas without distortion; unsupported resolutions fall back to the nearest known aspect.

nodes.label: ws_has_camera_access
nodes.rationale: Birdseye is a composite stream mixing every camera, so only roles with unrestricted access (admin or a role with no camera restriction list) may receive it; per-camera streams instead check the role's allowed camera set.

nodes.label: distance_to_score
nodes.rationale: Normalizes cosine distance with the ZScoreNormalization stats EmbeddingsContext already maintains so scores are comparable across deployments, then applies a bounded sigmoid. Uninitialized stats (stddev 0) return a neutral 0.5 so the raw-distance fallback ordering still dominates.

nodes.label: fuse_scores
nodes.rationale: Visual weight 0.65 dominates description weight 0.35 because the feature's primary use case is finding the same specific object. A missing side is returned alone with no penalty rather than penalizing events lacking a description embedding.

nodes.label: _sanitize_existing_image
nodes.rationale: sanitize_filepath normalizes backslashes but leaves '..' intact, so a path like clips\..\..\etc/passwd passes the CLIPS_DIR prefix check yet escapes the directory once resolved. A valid snapshot path never contains '..', so any is rejected.

nodes.label: _get_item_recording_export_errors
nodes.rationale: Groups batch items by camera and issues one query per unique camera covering that camera's full requested range, then checks each item's range in Python, avoiding O(N) DB round-trips on large batches.

nodes.label: chat_completion
nodes.rationale: The system message is generated only on the first turn and returned in the message chain so the client replays it verbatim, freezing its timestamp to keep the prompt prefix byte-identical and the model server's prompt cache hitting.

nodes.label: _execute_pending_tools
nodes.rationale: get_live_context results carry an _image_url that is popped and re-injected as a user message, because images cannot be sent inside tool-result messages.

nodes.label: Candidate-then-filter vector search pattern
nodes.rationale: Event ids are deliberately not passed into the sqlite-vec queries because the IN filter is broken in the installed version. Instead the top-k rows are fetched globally per modality and then intersected with the structured Peewee filters, the same pattern used by events_search.

nodes.label: _resolve_zones
nodes.rationale: LLMs echo the user's casing or a zone's friendly name instead of the configured key, but the downstream filter is a case-sensitive SQLite GLOB over the JSON zones column, so unnormalized names silently return zero matches.

nodes.label: latest_frame
nodes.rationale: Falls back to the most recent preview frame when the camera's last frame is older than its ffmpeg retry_interval, and finally to a bundled camera-error image, so the UI always renders something for an offline camera.

nodes.label: _resolve_cache_age
nodes.rationale: When a media handler is invoked directly by another handler instead of through its route, FastAPI never resolves the Query() default, so max_cache_age arrives as the Query object and its int default has to be unwrapped.

nodes.label: vod_ts
nodes.rationale: nginx-vod-module pushes clipFrom forward to the next keyframe, which can leave too few frames and produce an unplayable segment, so clipFrom is snapped back to the preceding keyframe and the duration adjusted.

nodes.label: get_preview_frames_from_cache
nodes.rationale: A camera's frames form a contiguous slice of the sorted listing, so bisect locates the range without scanning the whole preview_frames directory.

nodes.label: _get_preview_frame_listing
nodes.rationale: Caches the sorted preview_frames listing keyed on directory mtime, which bumps whenever a frame is added or removed, with a double-checked lock so a concurrent refresh is not repeated.

nodes.label: no_recordings
nodes.rationale: Merges overlapping recordings into covered intervals in a single ordered pass, then walks time segments with a moving index so gap detection stays linear rather than re-scanning the interval list per segment.

nodes.label: motion_activity
nodes.rationale: Resample emits a row for every bucket spanning the range; buckets with no recording get motion 0 and an empty camera string, so those gap-fill rows are dropped after normalization.

nodes.label: Thumbnail Payloads Moved Out of Event List Responses
Extension (image format enum with MIME mapping)
Verbatim Tool-Call Replay for Prompt Cache Hits
Case Attachment Admin-Only Until Case-Level ACLs Exist
Verbatim Conversation Replay for Prompt Cache
nodes.rationale: The full message chain including the system message is returned so the client can persist and replay it byte-identically on the next request; keeping the prompt prefix stable is what lets the model server's prompt cache keep hitting.

nodes.label: transform_is_finite
nodes.rationale: A near-singular homography (common when the motion estimator lacks stable features while zooming a low-texture scene) yields inf/nan matrix entries; norfair accumulates the homography across frames, so one bad transform poisons every later one and propagates nan into the tracker distance function, crashing the camera process. Bad transforms are dropped and the estimator is reset instead.

nodes.label: PtzAutoTracker._calibrate_camera
nodes.rationale: The camera is stepped from a preset in measured increments so a simple linear regression can predict movement times; predicted times let the tracker aim at where the object will be rather than where it was.

nodes.label: PtzAutoTracker._should_zoom_in
nodes.rationale: Zoom decisions use hysteresis thresholds (AUTOTRACKING_ZOOM_IN/OUT_HYSTERESIS) to prevent a yo-yo zooming effect, and refuse to zoom in while the box touches frame edges or the object moves quickly.

nodes.label: PtzAutoTracker.check_for_updates
nodes.rationale: Camera processes read ptz_metrics.autotracker_enabled instead of the config object, so every config path that can toggle autotracking must mirror its value into the metrics, not just the mqtt toggle that writes it directly.

nodes.label: Stale Detect-Resolution Batch Discard
nodes.rationale: When a camera's detect resolution changes, tracked state is dropped so old-grid boxes cannot leak through end-callbacks, and in-flight batches from the pre-recycle detect process whose boxes exceed the new resolution are skipped entirely.

nodes.label: Fast-Track Publish Threshold for Face/LPR
nodes.rationale: When the detection model has no built-in face/license_plate class, object-area multipliers (6x for faces, 20x for plates) start fast-tracking updates slightly before the optimal size zone, lowering the publish staleness threshold from 5s to 1s so secondary recognition pipelines get frames sooner.

nodes.label: Replay Camera Recycle on Config Refresh
nodes.rationale: Only replay cameras are recycled on a refresh update so detect width/height/fps propagate through ffmpeg args, SHM sizing, and the region grid; regular cameras still require a full Frigate restart for a detect change.

nodes.label: Deferred SHM Frame Slot Unlink
nodes.rationale: Unlinking the per-frame YUV segments is only safe after the capture/processor subprocesses are joined, since they no longer hold mappings; other long-lived processes keep their existing mappings until frame_manager.get sees a shape that no longer fits and reopens the stale ref.

nodes.label: Zone Label Rebuild on Runtime Config Change
nodes.rationale: Counters for zones that no longer exist are dropped and counters for new zones are pre-created so the first count after a runtime zones/objects change is actually published rather than being suppressed as unchanged.

nodes.label: create_detector
nodes.rationale: Single factory entry point: looks the detector class up in the plugin registry by config type rather than importing plugins directly, so unavailable hardware runtimes never have to be imported by callers.

nodes.label: DetectionApi abstract base
nodes.rationale: Every detector subclass declares type_key and implements detect_raw, which is how plugin auto-registration and the (20,6) detection contract are enforced across wildly different hardware backends.

nodes.label: DetectionApi.calculate_grids_strides
nodes.rationale: Shared YOLOX anchor grid/stride precomputation for strides 8/16/32; the expanded flag switches between flat concatenated grids (ONNX/OpenVINO) and per-level lists (RKNN).

nodes.label: 20x6 float32 detection array contract
nodes.rationale: Every detector returns a fixed np.zeros((20,6), float32) array ordered [class_id, score, y_min, x_min, y_max, x_max] with coordinates normalized to 0..1 and padded to exactly 20 rows, so the object detection process can treat all hardware backends identically and use a fixed-size shared memory buffer.

nodes.label: tflite_detect_raw
nodes.rationale: Shared SSD-style TFLite postprocess (boxes/class_ids/scores/count tensors) reused by the CPU and Teflon plugins so only the interpreter construction differs between them.

nodes.label: tflite_load_delegate_interpreter
nodes.rationale: A ValueError from load_delegate is ambiguous, so the handler inspects the model extension to tell the user whether the real problem is a non-.tflite model or a missing NPU.

nodes.label: api_types plugin registry
nodes.rationale: Plugins are discovered by walking the plugins package with pkgutil and registered via DetectionApi.__subclasses__(); import failures are logged and skipped because OpenVINO can fail to import on ARM devices with 64 KiB page size. DetectorTypeEnum and the discriminated DetectorConfig union are derived from the same discovery.

nodes.label: ModelTypeEnum
nodes.rationale: The model architecture enum (ssd, yolox, yolonas, yolo-generic, rfdetr, dfine) is the branch key every plugin's detect_raw and every runner capability check dispatches on.

nodes.label: ModelConfig.check_and_load_plus_model
nodes.rationale: plus:// paths are resolved by downloading the model and its JSON metadata into the model cache once, then overwriting width/height/tensor/pixel-format/type from server metadata so Frigate+ models never need manual config. RKNN is force-overridden to NHWC.

nodes.label: BaseDetectorConfig
nodes.rationale: extra=allow plus a per-plugin Literal type field lets each plugin subclass add its own fields while pydantic discriminates the union on type.

nodes.label: BaseModelRunner
nodes.rationale: One runner interface (get_input_names/get_input_width/run) lets detectors and embedding models share hardware backends without knowing which runtime was selected.

nodes.label: get_optimized_runner
nodes.rationale: Backend selection ladder: RKNN auto-conversion first, then OpenVINO only when ORT falls back to CPUExecutionProvider (there is no way to prioritize OpenVINO over CUDA/ROCm images), then CUDA graphs for supported models, and MIGraphX is dropped for models it cannot compile.

nodes.label: ONNXModelRunner
nodes.rationale: Holds an optional inference lock because JinaV2 shares one runner between text and vision embeddings called from different threads.

nodes.label: CudaGraphRunner
nodes.rationale: Captures a CUDA graph on first run via IOBinding then replays it with update_inplace; CUDA graphs limit supported operations so CLIP, PaddleOCR, YOLO-NAS and D-FINE are excluded.

nodes.label: OpenVINOModelRunner
nodes.rationale: Falls back from NPU to GPU for unsupported model types, sets NPU_TURBO for detection models, and recreates the infer_request per call for ArcFace because reused request state pollutes face embedding results.

nodes.label: _OPENVINO_LOCK
nodes.rationale: Process-wide lock serializing every OpenVINO compile and inference call, covering both the shared-runner JinaV2 case and distinct runners on separate threads such as the ArcFace face-model build versus the LPR detector.

nodes.label: RKNNModelRunner
nodes.rationale: Infers input names and widths from the model filename because RKNN blobs carry no usable metadata, transposes NCHW to NHWC, and de-normalizes ArcFace input back to uint8 since the RKNN runtime applies mean/std internally.

nodes.label: TensorRtDetector
nodes.rationale: Deliberately refuses to run on x86_64 and directs users to the ONNX detector; retained only for Nvidia Jetson. Binding accessors branch on TRT_VERSION < 10 to support both the legacy binding API and the newer tensor API.

nodes.label: HostDeviceMem
nodes.rationale: Pairs pinned host memory with its device pointer so inference can memcpy asynchronously; frees both in __del__ to avoid leaking CUDA allocations across detector restarts.

nodes.label: Rknn detector
nodes.rationale: Distinguishes user models (path contains a slash, optionally auto-converted from ONNX) from preset names matched against regex patterns, whose RKNN blobs follow the origin-quant-basename-soc-tkversion-rev naming scheme and are downloaded per SoC.

nodes.label: SynapDetector
nodes.rationale: Import of the Synap SDK is guarded by SYNAP_SUPPORT so the plugin module still registers on non-Synaptics images; only .synap models are accepted and only SSD output is decoded.

nodes.label: TeflonTfl detector
nodes.rationale: Uses Debian's mesa-teflon-delegate at /usr/lib/teflon/libteflon.so; the _tfl key suffix marks it as defaulting to a tflite model.

nodes.label: CpuTfl detector
nodes.rationale: Interpreter construction is wrapped in suppress_stderr_during because TFLite delegate creation messages bypass Python logging.

nodes.label: Axengine detector
nodes.rationale: Only preset frigate-yolov9-* .axmodel names are accepted; matching models are downloaded from the AXERA-TECH HuggingFace repo into a local axengine cache.

nodes.label: EdgeTpuTfl detector
nodes.rationale: Output tensor ordering and names are unreliable on compiled EdgeTPU models, so boxes vs class-score tensors are identified by shape (last dim 64 means DFL boxes), with a documented failure mode when a model has exactly 64 classes.

nodes.label: EdgeTpuTfl.detect_raw
nodes.rationale: Filters candidates while still quantized and defers sigmoid until after NMS to cut post-processing cost; logit scores are shifted positive because cv2.dnn.NMSBoxes requires a non-negative score threshold.

nodes.label: OvDetector
nodes.rationale: Validates model input/output arity and shapes at load time and sets model_invalid so detect_raw returns empty detections instead of crashing the detection process on a misconfigured model.

nodes.label: ZmqIpcDetector
nodes.rationale: REQ/REP over IPC with a multipart [header_json, tensor_bytes] protocol; send and receive timeouts plus socket recreation keep a stalled external inference process from blocking the detection loop, and every error path returns a preallocated zero (20,6) result.

nodes.label: ZmqIpcDetector._check_and_transfer_model
nodes.rationale: Model availability check and transfer are one atomic exchange, with the receive timeout temporarily raised to 30s because loading a model on the remote side can take seconds.

nodes.label: DeepStack detector
nodes.rationale: Encodes each frame as JPEG and posts it to a remote DeepStack/CodeProject.AI HTTP endpoint; truck is remapped to car so remote label vocabularies line up with Frigate's labelmap.

nodes.label: ONNXDetector._warmup
nodes.rationale: Runs one dummy inference during detector construction to front-load CUDA PTX JIT (Blackwell) and MIGraphX graph compilation, keeping the watchdog start_time at 0.0 so the detection process is not killed on first real frame.

nodes.label: HailoDetector
nodes.rationale: Detects the Hailo architecture with hailortcli and downloads a default yolov6n HEF from the Hailo model zoo when no model path is configured; detect_raw is synchronous over an async engine and returns zeros on timeout, raising only if the inference thread has died.

nodes.label: HailoAsyncInference
nodes.rationale: hailo_platform is imported lazily inside __init__ because importing it activates the driver and leaves processes running even when the detector is unused.

nodes.label: MemryXDetector
nodes.rationale: Fully asynchronous detector: detect_raw is a stub returning 0 and inference flows through send_input/process_input/process_output queues driven by the MemryX AsyncAccl callbacks. Model DFPs are fetched as zip archives from developer.memryx.com and cached under a FileLock so concurrent detector processes do not race on extraction.

nodes.label: MemryXDetector.post_process_yolo_optimized
nodes.rationale: Pure NumPy DFL decode plus NMS for YOLOv9, written to avoid the cropped ONNX post-processing sections that MemryX otherwise runs on CPU.

nodes.label: clear_orphaned_comments
nodes.rationale: When a deletion empties a ruamel collection, stranded comment tokens are emitted above a dedented flow-style {} and corrupt the config, so the emptied collection's comment metadata is cleared while non-empty siblings keep theirs.

nodes.label: cosine_distance
nodes.rationale: Reimplemented in numpy specifically to match sqlite-vec's cosine calculation so in-process scores agree with vector index results.

nodes.label: clear_and_unlink
nodes.rationale: File contents are truncated before unlink so space held by lingering file descriptors is actually released (frigate issue 4769).

nodes.label: xyxy_to_xywh_for_nms
nodes.rationale: cv2.dnn.NMSBoxes reads the last two values as width/height, so passing corner coordinates inflates every box toward the bottom-right and suppresses valid neighboring detections.

nodes.label: get_ort_providers
nodes.rationale: TensorRT is opt-in because it consumes too much memory without tuning, and Azure is skipped entirely since it is never present on local hardware yet would block fallback to OpenVINO when listed first.

nodes.label: get_audio_from_recording
nodes.rationale: Builds an ffmpeg concat playlist with inpoint/outpoint so recording segments that straddle the requested window are trimmed, and emits 16 kHz mono PCM WAV to match sherpa-onnx input.

nodes.label: get_camera_regions_grid
nodes.rationale: Learns expected region sizes per 8x8 grid cell from historical timeline boxes so detection regions match how large objects actually appear in each part of the frame.

nodes.label: get_cluster_candidates
nodes.rationale: Boxes smaller than 5% of the resulting region are not clustered, otherwise a small object would be downscaled into invisibility inside an oversized shared region.

nodes.label: reduce_detections
nodes.rationale: Clipped detections get their confidence floored at 0.6 rather than dropped, so an object cut by a region edge still survives NMS instead of losing to a duplicate.

nodes.label: SharedMemoryFrameManager
nodes.rationale: get() drops a cached segment whose size no longer matches the requested shape, because a same-name shared memory recreate would otherwise hand back a stale or mid-recreate buffer.

nodes.label: UntrackedSharedMemory
nodes.rationale: Temporarily patches multiprocessing.resource_tracker.register so segments are not auto-unlinked by the tracker (CPython issue 82300); a lock guards the global patch against other threads.

nodes.label: is_better_thumbnail
nodes.rationale: Face on a person and license_plate on a car outrank raw score and area, so a thumbnail that already carries the identifying attribute is only replaced by a better one.

nodes.label: is_rknn_compatible
nodes.rationale: The SoC string is checked against SUPPORTED_RK_SOCS because /proc/device-tree/compatible can exist with non-RK content (for example macOS Docker) and would otherwise produce a false positive.

nodes.label: get_config_schema
nodes.rationale: Pydantic's default schema for Dict[str, BaseDetectorConfig] exposes only base-class fields, so the detectors property is repointed at the polymorphic DetectorConfig union to surface every detector plugin's schema.

nodes.label: run_ffmpeg_with_progress
nodes.rationale: Stdout stays attached to the parent to avoid buffer-full deadlocks, and the process is niced to low priority so long concats do not starve detection.

nodes.label: get_event_snapshot_path
nodes.rationale: Legacy JPG snapshots may already contain burned-in overlays, so they are never returned when a clean image is requested for further rendering.

nodes.label: ModelDownloader._download_models
nodes.rationale: Existence is re-checked inside the file lock so two processes racing on the same model file do not both download it.

nodes.label: ModelDownloader.download_from_url
nodes.rationale: Downloads to a .part file and renames on success so a partial transfer is never mistaken for a complete model.

nodes.label: Media sync safety threshold
nodes.rationale: Any sync that would delete more than 50% of files or DB rows aborts by default, on the assumption that a mass mismatch is a misconfigured storage path rather than genuine orphans; force=True is the explicit override.

nodes.label: SqliteVecQueueDatabase
nodes.rationale: Extends peewee's SqliteQueueDatabase so every new connection loads the sqlite-vec extension and registers a timeout-bounded REGEXP function, keeping vector search and regex filters available to all queries.

nodes.label: SqliteVecQueueDatabase._register_regexp
nodes.rationale: REGEXP is bounded by a 1 second timeout and swallows regex errors so a malicious or pathological user pattern cannot hang the shared database queue thread.

nodes.label: SqliteVecQueueDatabase._delete_embeddings
nodes.rationale: Embeddings outlive the events they belong to when semantic search is disabled, so deletes are attempted regardless of current config, guarded by a sqlite_master existence check because the vec0 tables only exist once semantic search has run.

nodes.label: SqliteVecQueueDatabase.create_embeddings_tables
nodes.rationale: vec0 virtual tables with FLOAT[768] cosine distance define the embedding contract shared by thumbnail and description search.

nodes.label: ONNX model download and state reporting lifecycle
Role to camera-list access model
nodes.rationale: auth.roles maps a role name to a list of allowed cameras, where an empty list means all cameras. 'admin' and 'viewer' are reserved and force-reset to empty lists after validation so a user config can never narrow the built-in roles, while custom roles are required to name at least one camera so an accidental empty list does not silently grant full access.

nodes.label: FFmpeg Command Recreation On Config Change
DataProcessorMetrics
nodes.rationale: Speed/rate counters are allocated as multiprocessing manager Value/dict proxies so separate Frigate processes can publish and read enrichment metrics without shared memory of their own.

nodes.label: Early GenAI request on significant updates
Whisper vs Sherpa-ONNX Model Size Selection
Lazy faster_whisper Import For AVX Safety
Per-process Whisper vs shared sherpa stream
Embedding delete tolerates missing vec0 tables
nodes.rationale: Event cleanup deletes embeddings whether or not semantic search is enabled, so the delete path must tolerate databases where the vec0 tables were never created and installs where the sqlite-vec extension is unavailable (in which case the writes are skipped entirely).

nodes.label: Fail-closed MQTT topic routing
nodes.rationale: Per-camera notification set/suspend topics must be registered with message_callback_add or paho silently drops them; camera-level notifications must also enable the global set topic, matching WebPushClient gating in app.py, but a disabled camera must not enable it.

nodes.label: Deferred Config Factory Reads Through Holder
Two-phase profile activation
nodes.rationale: apply_profile_to_config mutates config only (no ZMQ, MQTT, or disk writes) because workers are started with the corrected values; activate_profile owns the bookkeeping and broadcast. Re-deriving the same state must still publish every section, because processes started before the config was corrected have no other channel. Startup replays pass clear_runtime_overrides=False so runtime overrides layered on top survive, and a config/set save relies on clear_runtime_state_for_yaml_keys instead of a broad wipe that would drop overrides for unrelated cameras. Profile changes also republish retained MQTT switch states so Home Assistant does not show a stale toggle.

nodes.label: Profile overrides must reference existing base entities
nodes.rationale: A profile may only override zones and motion masks that exist on the base camera, and may only reference profiles declared at the top level; phantom names are rejected at parse time rather than silently creating new entities at activation.

nodes.label: Orphaned comments on emptied yaml collections
nodes.rationale: Deleting the last key of a commented map, or the last item of a commented sequence, leaves ruamel emitting orphaned comment tokens above a flow-style {} or [] at column 0, which is unparseable yaml. The comments attached to the removed entry must be stripped from the file, while comments on surviving sibling keys and on updated values are preserved.

nodes.label: Shared threshold singletons
nodes.rationale: get_stationary_threshold runs per object per frame, so an unknown label must return the shared DEFAULT_OBJECT_THRESHOLDS instance rather than allocating a fresh StationaryThresholds each call; the shared default stays value-equivalent to a fresh instance.

nodes.label: PasswordDigest to PasswordText fallback
nodes.rationale: A WS-Security Fault means the encoding was rejected, so retry once with PasswordText and surface the original digest Fault if both fail. Transport-level errors (timeout, refused, unreachable) must propagate immediately so probing does not double its latency. HTTP digest auth is a separate axis and replaces each service's zeep transport.

nodes.label: Birdseye requires unrestricted role
nodes.rationale: Birdseye composites every camera, so a role restricted to a camera subset must be denied the birdseye JSMPEG stream; only roles with no camera restriction may view it.

nodes.label: Startup-only autotracker state
nodes.rationale: Per-camera autotracker state was built once at construction and never revisited: autotracker_init only had entries for cameras enabled at that moment, so a runtime-added or runtime-enabled camera raised KeyError and killed the autotracker thread for every camera; and ptz_metrics.autotracker_enabled, which camera processes actually read, was never updated on a config save so the tracker never built a motion estimator. Metric sync must also tolerate a camera whose metrics do not exist yet, since add reaches the maintainer and the autotracker on separate threads with no ordering guarantee.

nodes.label: Role map OR semantics
nodes.rationale: A separator-joined proxy role header is matched with OR semantics against each role's group list, whitespace-trimmed and case-insensitive for direct role names; an unmatched or empty header falls back to default_role rather than granting nothing or granting too much.

nodes.label: Runtime state to YAML key mapping
nodes.rationale: Only tracked topics are persisted (untracked ones such as ptz_autotracker are a no-op and must not even create the file), a corrupt or unexpectedly shaped JSON file degrades to empty rather than raising, and clearing is keyed off the YAML paths a config save rewrote so unrelated cameras keep their overrides. The camera-level enabled topic maps to the top-level cameras.<cam>.enabled key rather than a nested .enabled.

nodes.label: Internal/external port collision auth bypass
nodes.rationale: nginx would accept the same port on different addresses as distinct listeners, but the /auth endpoint decides trust on the port alone, so the external listener would inherit anonymous admin access. Validation rejects identical ports regardless of bind address.

nodes.label: init=True implies request objects exist
nodes.rationale: In the normal wizard flow ONVIF is set up before autotracking is enabled. Autotracking-only request objects used to be created only when autotracking was on at init time, leaving init=True with no status_request; get_camera_status skips its re-init branch when init is True and then raised KeyError on the tracking thread. The requests come from the locally parsed WSDL and cost no network, so they are always built. Inversely, manual relative moves must not write ptz movement timestamps for a non-autotracking camera, because only camera_maintenance polls get_camera_status to clear them, and a stuck clock suppresses promotion of motion boxes to detection regions, stopping object detection entirely.

nodes.label: Tool Call Arguments Must Be Dicts
REGEXP ReDoS timeout (GHSA-q8jx-q884-jcq9)
nodes.rationale: An attacker-controlled catastrophic pattern reaching the REGEXP sink backtracks for minutes to hours and wedges the serialized database worker thread, so REGEXP evaluation is time-bounded by REGEXP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS. Invalid patterns and NULL values return false instead of raising.

nodes.label: NMS box format regression suite
nodes.rationale: cv2.dnn.NMSBoxes expects [x, y, width, height]; passing corner coordinates makes OpenCV read x2/y2 as width/height, inflating every box toward the bottom-right proportional to its distance from the origin. Two well separated objects far from the origin then appear to overlap (IoU 0.465 > 0.4 threshold) and the lower scoring one is silently suppressed. Fixed geometry A=(393,499,484,620) B=(527,499,618,620) at 640x640 pins the bug across every detector post-processor.

nodes.label: Quiet Segment Drop Under Motion Retention
Stale SHM cache invalidation
nodes.rationale: A same-name SHM segment can be unlinked and recreated at a different size across a camera add/remove or resolution change while a long-lived in-process cache (e.g. TrackedObjectProcessor) still holds the old ref. A too-small cached ref makes np.ndarray raise 'buffer is too small'; a too-large one passes any size check but points at an orphaned inode whose stale bytes get reinterpreted at the new shape, producing miscolored distorted YUV. Both must drop the cache and reopen by name; if the reopened segment is still too small (maintainer mid-recreate) skip the frame and do not cache it. Size must be computed with np.prod so n-dimensional shapes work.

nodes.label: Idle vs Error GPU Sampling States
NaN distance guard
nodes.rationale: norfair raises a hard ValueError on any nan distance, killing the camera process. An ill-conditioned homography during autotracking can hand the tracker non-finite, zero-area, or corner-inverted estimate boxes, so distance() must return inf rather than nan. A positive-only guard is insufficient because nan <= 0 is False.

nodes.label: Runtime state replay after config swap
ZMQ topic-prefixed JSON wire format
nodes.rationale: Messages are sent as a single string 'topic_base+topic+sub_topic <json>' so ZMQ prefix subscription (SUBSCRIBE on topic_base) does the routing in the broker rather than in Python; subscribers split on the first space and json-decode the remainder.

nodes.label: NorfairTracker
nodes.rationale: Per-object-type Kalman configs (car, license_plate, PTZ person) exist because a single R/Q pair mistracks both fast vehicles and near-static plates; lowering R trusts bounding box position over prediction.

nodes.label: distance (size-normalized box distance)
nodes.rationale: Distance is normalized by estimated object size so a fixed threshold works across near and far objects; width/height ratios are folded into the change vector to penalize shape drift.

nodes.label: NorfairTracker._create_tracker
nodes.rationale: Re-id parameters are only attached when stationary max_frames is None, because objects that never expire are the ones that need appearance-based recovery after occlusion.

nodes.label: Per-class stationary threshold sets
nodes.rationale: Objects are bucketed into stationary (bbq_grill, package, waste_bin), dynamic (vehicles), and non-stationary (license_plate) sets because one IoU sensitivity cannot serve both a parked car and a plate that must never latch as stationary.

nodes.label: StationaryMotionClassifier
nodes.rationale: Compares a fixed spatial region (historical median box) across frames rather than the current detection box, so bounding box jitter cannot flip a truly stationary object to active.

nodes.label: TrackedObject.update
nodes.rationale: Only new attribute labels flag a significant change; disappearance is ignored because detection skips stationary objects on non-interval frames and would otherwise emit spurious updates.

nodes.label: TrackedObjectAttribute.find_best_object
nodes.rationale: When several objects contain the same attribute box the smaller object wins (a person in front of a car), and two overlapping objects of the same label yield no assignment at all.

nodes.label: EXTENDED_LOITERING_OBJECTS
nodes.rationale: Person is treated as always actively loitering because a loitering alert must persist even while the person stays motionless, unlike a car that legitimately parks.

nodes.label: validate_ffmpeg_args
nodes.rationale: Every token must be an allowlisted flag or its value, and no token may become a bare input/output URL, which structurally prevents arbitrary file read/write, network exfiltration/SSRF, and resource exhaustion through the export endpoint. Admin users are trusted and skip validation.

nodes.label: RecordingExporter._build_chapter_metadata_file
nodes.rationale: The VOD endpoint concatenates recording clips back to back, so wall-clock gaps collapse in the produced video; chapter offsets must therefore be computed in output time by walking the same recording rows that build the playlist.

nodes.label: RecordingExporter._build_recording_segment_chapter_metadata_file
nodes.rationale: One ISO 8601 chapter per recording segment lets a viewer map any playback position back to real-world time without OCR-ing a burnt-in timestamp.

nodes.label: RecordingExporter._expected_output_duration_seconds
nodes.rationale: Users often request a wide time range when only a few minutes of recordings exist on disk, so progress based on the requested range plateaus early; actual saved seconds are summed from Recordings/Previews and scaled by the timelapse setpts factor.

nodes.label: RecordingCleanup.truncate_wal
nodes.rationale: SQLite normally checkpoints the WAL automatically, but sustained high activity can starve the checkpoint so the WAL grows without bound; a manual TRUNCATE checkpoint is forced once it exceeds MAX_WAL_SIZE.

nodes.label: Frigate Devcontainer Definition
nodes.rationale: Pins the VS Code toolchain (Ruff, ESLint, Prettier, Pylance) and forwards the Frigate port set (8971 external nginx, 5000 internal nginx, 5001 API, 5173 Vite, 8554 RTSP, 8555 WebRTC); CUDA/ONNX GPU features are commented out as opt-in.

nodes.label: Devcontainer post_create.sh
nodes.rationale: Creates /media/frigate owned by the host user because the devcontainer runs non-root unlike the normal container, and exports LIBAVFORMAT_VERSION_MAJOR in .bashrc since interactive dev shells lack the s6 service file that normally defines it.

nodes.label: Devcontainer initialize.sh
nodes.rationale: Runs on the host before container creation so debug/ and web/dist exist owned by the host user, and seeds config/config.yml from the example without clobbering an existing one.

nodes.label: ONNX Runtime GPU Devcontainer Feature
nodes.rationale: Declares installsAfter the nvidia-cuda feature so the CUDA toolkit is present before onnxruntime-gpu is pip installed.

nodes.label: MobileNetEmbedder
nodes.rationale: Contamination analysis deliberately uses a fixed ImageNet-pretrained MobileNetV2 backbone rather than the user's trained classifier, because the trained model may have memorized contaminating images into the correct class and would hide them in its own embedding space.

nodes.label: Upsampling Blob Quarantine
nodes.rationale: Crops under 80x80 are stretched 3-7x to the 224x224 classifier input and collapse into a similar feature-space region regardless of identity, so quarantining them often fixes feature collapse. Caveat: when the target naturally appears small at the camera distance, those crops ARE the inference-time input and removing them collapses named-class accuracy, so restore the quarantine and review individual crops instead.

nodes.label: None Class Requirement
nodes.rationale: Without a well-populated 'none' class the classifier has no 'I don't know' option, so every unknown runtime crop is forced into a real class. Target a count comparable to the other classes, images at least 100x100, and visual variety. Class balance skew above 3x also lets the dominant class absorb borderline predictions.

nodes.label: Degenerate Embedding Signature
nodes.rationale: When neg-to-neg cosine similarity exceeds pos-to-pos similarity, the negatives are not per-identity embeddings at all: upsampled tiny crops collapse into a common 'face-like blob' region of embedding space regardless of who the face belongs to, which is why low-resolution runtime crops produce confident false positives.

nodes.label: Filename-Time Seek Convention
nodes.rationale: Frigate catalogs recording segments by the UTC wall-clock time encoded in the path (YYYY-MM-DD/HH/camera/MM.SS.mp4) and treats that filename time as PTS=0 for seek math, so any offset between filename time and the first packet PTS becomes seek imprecision. Long or irregular GOPs (max gap > 5s) from adaptive/smart codecs compound the error even when 'Smart Codec' is off in the camera UI.

nodes.label: Jetson nvmpi ffmpeg build rationale
nodes.rationale: NVIDIA ships a Jetson ffmpeg deb with accelerated decoding only, so Frigate builds ffmpeg 6.0 from source with the jetson-ffmpeg nvmpi patch to get accelerated scaling and encoding. dGPU codecs (cuvid/nvenc/nvdec) are explicitly disabled while nvmpi and ffnvcodec are enabled, because the Jetson uses the tegra multimedia path rather than a discrete GPU. Stub libs are used at build time since the tegra multimedia libraries are not present in the build image.

nodes.label: python-tensorrt self-build rationale
nodes.rationale: NVIDIA only publishes python-tensorrt bindings for python3.10 on arm64, but the Frigate image runs python3.11, so the TensorRT 8.6 bindings wheel is compiled from source against python3.11 headers.

nodes.label: Hailo-8L Host Driver Installer
nodes.rationale: Builds and installs the hailort PCIe kernel driver on the host (not in the container) at pinned version 4.21.0, because the accelerator needs a host kernel module and firmware in /lib/firmware/hailo. Explicitly diagnoses Secure Boot key rejection as the common modprobe failure, and installs dkms only on trixie.

nodes.label: OpenVINO SSDLite Model Converter
nodes.rationale: Replaces the legacy openvino-dev Model Optimizer with a hand-built conversion. The TensorFlow frontend translates the Object Detection API pre and post processors literally, producing per-class NonMaxSuppression, NonZero and Loop ops with data dependent shapes that the GPU plugin handles very badly. The preprocessor is bypassed as an identity at the native 300x300 input and the postprocessor is replaced by a single fused DetectionOutput, reproducing what ssd_v2_support.json used to do. Anchors are folded to a constant since they depend only on the static input shape. Build-time asserts fail the image rather than silently shipping a dynamically shaped graph.

nodes.label: Base Image Dependency Installer
nodes.rationale: Installs three parallel ffmpeg builds (5.0, 7.0, 8.0) per architecture so camera-specific regressions can be worked around by selecting a version at runtime. Layers Intel GPU support from multiple sources: jammy repo for legacy libmfx1, trixie for libva2/libvpl2/libmfx-gen1.2 for Battlemage, and pinned .deb releases for both legacy and current compute-runtime plus NPU level-zero drivers. Symlinks iHD_drv_video.so to xe_drv_video.so because Battlemage uses the xe kernel driver while the VA-API driver is still iHD.

nodes.label: Pinned Upstream Artifact Fetching
nodes.rationale: Nearly every accelerator and codec dependency is fetched as a pinned GitHub release URL (edgetpu, ffmpeg builds, compute-runtime, level-zero, NPU driver, hailort, memryx, s6-overlay) instead of from distro repos, because the required versions are newer or not packaged at all. The cost is manual version bumps; the benefit is reproducible builds independent of Debian's release cadence.

nodes.label: MemryX Accelerator Installer
nodes.rationale: Unpacks the mx_accl_frigate 2.1.0 release into /opt and symlinks the memryx package into site-packages resolved at runtime, so the install survives Python minor version changes. Copies x86 or arm shared libraries into the arch-specific lib dir and runs ldconfig; unsupported architectures fail loudly.

nodes.label: Intel Media Driver Build Script
nodes.rationale: Builds gmmlib 22.7.2 and intel-media-driver 25.2.6 from source into /rootfs because Debian's packaged driver lacks Battlemage (Xe2) support. Uses Intel's jammy repo for libva-dev 2.22, which supplies the VVC decode headers media-driver 25.x needs. On non-x86_64 it creates an empty /rootfs so the downstream Dockerfile COPY --from still has a valid source.

nodes.label: sqlite-vec Loadable Module Build Script
nodes.rationale: Builds sqlite-vec 0.1.9 as a loadable extension (vec0) against a vendored SQLite amalgamation, giving Frigate vector search inside its existing SQLite database instead of adding a separate vector store dependency.

nodes.label: s6-overlay Installer
nodes.rationale: Extracts s6-overlay 3.2.1.0 noarch plus the arch-specific tarball into /rootfs so the Dockerfile can COPY --from a single staged tree. s6 provides the multi-process supervision Frigate's container needs (frigate, nginx, go2rtc).

nodes.label: /rootfs Staging Pattern for COPY --from
nodes.rationale: Builder stages install their artifacts into /rootfs rather than the real filesystem so the final Dockerfile stage can COPY --from a single tree without dragging in build toolchains. The Intel media driver script creates an empty /rootfs on non-x86_64 purely so that COPY --from never fails on architectures where the stage is a no-op.

nodes.label: Nginx Build Script (VOD + secure token)
nodes.rationale: Compiles nginx 1.27.4 from source with kaltura's nginx-vod-module and nginx-secure-token-module plus ngx_devel_kit and set-misc, none of which ship in distro packages. MAX_CLIPS is patched from 128 to 1080 so long recording playlists can be served, and avc_hevc_parser_rbsp_trailing_bits is patched to return TRUE early to work around frigate issue 4572. ccache is used to cut rebuild time.

nodes.label: pysqlite3 Wheel Build Script
nodes.rationale: Builds a statically linked pysqlite3 0.5.3 wheel against the SQLite 3.46.1 amalgamation so Frigate is not bound to the base image's system SQLite (which varies across base images such as NVIDIA TensorRT). Fetches the pre-built amalgamation rather than compiling SQLite from source to save build time.

nodes.label: Vendored SQLite Amalgamation Strategy
nodes.rationale: Both the Python driver and the vector extension are compiled against a downloaded sqlite.org amalgamation zip rather than the distro libsqlite3, so behavior and feature flags are identical across every base image and architecture Frigate ships.

nodes.label: HailoRT Runtime Installer (container)
nodes.rationale: Pulls prebuilt hailort 4.21.0 tarballs and cp311 wheels from the frigate-nvr/hailort fork rather than building in-image, keeping the version locked to the same 4.21.0 the host driver installer builds.

nodes.label: go2rtc restricted source policy (echo/expr/exec)
nodes.rationale: Stream sources using echo/expr/exec, and the map form ({"url": ...}) which go2rtc resolves recursively and can therefore only be backed by an exec source, are stripped from the generated config by default because they allow arbitrary command execution. Operators must explicitly opt in with GO2RTC_ALLOW_ARBITRARY_EXEC=true. Offending streams are deleted rather than passed through so a misconfiguration fails closed.

nodes.label: go2rtc default CORS and hass config defaults
nodes.rationale: api.origin defaults to '*' so the Frigate Home Assistant integration and the frigate-card work without manual go2rtc configuration; hass.config defaults to /homeassistant; log.format defaults to text so logs stay readable.

nodes.label: Migration 014: add score / model provenance fields
Anonymous Review Identity
nodes.rationale: Migration 030 backfills review status for every username plus a synthetic 'anonymous' user so unauthenticated viewers keep a review state after has_been_reviewed moves off reviewsegment; raw SQL is used for the backfill to avoid ORM issues with columns that do not exist yet, and rollback restores the column without data.

nodes.label: Migration 015: relax event columns, add JSON data blob
generateTsFile
nodes.rationale: Emits AUTO-GENERATED TypeScript from config.yaml so the Docker Compose Generator data has a single YAML source of truth plus a typed lookup Map for id access.

nodes.label: Table vs Step-List UI Pattern Choice
ALL_CONFIG_SECTIONS
nodes.rationale: Navigation tables are hardcoded from web/src/pages/Settings.tsx and views/settings.json menu labels, so the doc generator does not have to parse the React router.

nodes.label: load_section_configs
nodes.rationale: Reads TypeScript section-config files with regex rather than a TS parser, accepting brittleness in exchange for a pure-Python doc toolchain with no Node dependency.

nodes.label: js-yaml Webpack Loader
nodes.rationale: Compiles YAML into a default-exported JS object so docs data can be authored in YAML (block scalars, no quote/newline escaping) yet imported exactly like the JSON it replaces.

nodes.label: yaml-data-loader Docusaurus Plugin
nodes.rationale: Scoped by include path to docs/data so it never intercepts other .yaml files such as the OpenAPI spec under static/.

nodes.label: getIconType (emoji vs image vs inline SVG)
toCssVars (style object to CSS custom properties)
TensorRT uses deploy reservations instead of /dev/dri passthrough
Always-rendered FAQ answer with CSS-only mobile collapse
nodes.rationale: The answer is always in the DOM and the desktop/mobile split is pure CSS at the 996px Docusaurus breakpoint, so there is no hydration flash and search engines plus the docs AI bot can read the answer regardless of collapsed state. The heading id resolves deep links on both layouts; toggling uses history.replaceState so an opened answer is shareable without history spam or an abrupt scroll.

nodes.label: SHM sizing formula
nodes.rationale: Shared memory per camera is (width * height * 1.5 * 20 + 270480) / 1048576 MB: 1.5 bytes/pixel for yuv420p, a 20 frame ring, plus fixed per-camera overhead, with a flat +40MB added once for logs. The inputs are the detect stream resolution rather than the record resolution because only detect frames are placed in shared memory; going above 720p is warned against since it costs SHM and CPU without improving detection accuracy.

nodes.label: Hand-rolled admonition rendering
nodes.rationale: marked does not understand Docusaurus admonition syntax (:::warning ... :::), so the component splits the markdown on an admonition regex, renders those blocks itself into styled divs, and hands everything else to marked. Fenced code is separately promoted to @theme/CodeBlock so it keeps syntax highlighting and the copy button.

nodes.label: Frigate Trademark Policy
nodes.rationale: Separates the MIT-licensed code from the unlicensed brand: forks must rename and drop the logo to avoid user confusion, and common law rights are asserted despite the absence of a registration symbol.

nodes.label: Contributing to Frigate
nodes.rationale: A PR is framed as a request for long-term maintenance, not just code; large features must be discussed before implementation because the long-term cost, not the implementation quality, is the gating factor.

nodes.label: Weblate Translation Workflow
nodes.rationale: Translations are edited in Weblate and auto-synced to the repo; PRs for translation changes are refused so translations stay tracked and coordinated in one system.

nodes.label: Frigate NVR (Product)
nodes.rationale: Local realtime NVR for IP cameras. Design intent: minimize resource use by running low-overhead motion detection first and only running object detection when and where necessary; heavy multiprocessing prioritizes realtime over processing every frame.

nodes.label: Devcontainer Docker Compose Stack
nodes.rationale: Defines the devcontainer service plus a no-auth Mosquitto MQTT broker; host render/video/plugdev group IDs must be added explicitly or OpenVINO GPU acceleration fails.

nodes.label: Frigate AI Policy
nodes.rationale: Written because unreviewed AI output costs unpaid maintainers real review time and gives less signal than a few honest sentences; the policy targets what is posted, not which tools were used.

nodes.label: Human In The Loop Requirement
nodes.source_location: ## A person has to be in the loop
nodes.rationale: Every issue, discussion, comment and PR must be read and submitted by a person. Bots/agents posting autonomously are prohibited because merged code creates a permanent maintenance burden that requires someone who understands it; code nobody understands is a liability.

nodes.label: AI Usage Disclosure Requirement
nodes.rationale: Disclosure is explicitly non-disqualifying: maintainers prefer honest disclosure over later discovery because trust matters more than method. Scrutiny scales inversely with a contributor's track record rather than through a formal exemption.

nodes.label: AI Policy Enforcement and Misjudgment Recourse
nodes.rationale: Maintainers acknowledge no reliable AI detection exists; calls are subjective and fast because volume is real. A contributor's word that they wrote it themselves is accepted, preferring occasional reopening over treating everyone as a suspect.

nodes.label: Audio Event Labelmap
nodes.rationale: Index-to-label mapping for the audio classification model (YAMNet-style classes collapsed into coarser labels such as 'speech' and 'yell').

nodes.label: COCO Object Labelmap
nodes.rationale: Index-to-label mapping for the object detector; note index 7 remaps 'truck' to 'car' so trucks and cars are treated as one class.

nodes.label: Login HTML Entry
nodes.rationale: Login is a separate Rollup entry point rather than a route so an unauthenticated user loads a minimal bundle and the main app bundle stays behind auth.

nodes.label: Frigate Web Frontend README
nodes.rationale: Dev server proxies to an existing Frigate instance via PROXY_HOST so the React frontend can be developed without rebuilding the Python backend; defaults to localhost:5000.

nodes.label: Dependabot Configuration
nodes.rationale: All ecosystems (actions, docker, pip for main/tensorrt, npm for web/docs) target the dev branch rather than a release branch; the docs npm ecosystem is narrowed to @docusaurus/* to limit PR noise.

nodes.label: Pull Request Template
nodes.rationale: Encodes the AI policy as required checkboxes (tool used, how, extent, human oversight) plus 'I can explain every line of code in this PR if asked', converting policy prose into a submission gate.

nodes.label: Support Intake Funnel
nodes.rationale: Blank issues are disabled and both contact links point at Discussions rather than Issues, so all bug reports and support requests are routed into categorized discussion templates first. Issues are reserved for triaged, confirmed work, keeping the issue tracker a work queue instead of a support inbox.

nodes.label: CI Workflow (multi-arch image builds)
nodes.rationale: Concurrency is grouped on github.ref with cancel-in-progress so only the latest commit builds, avoiding registry cache overwrites. The default multi-arch manifest is assembled from the amd64 image plus the RPi image rather than the generic arm64 image, because the majority of arm64 users are Raspberry Pi users.

nodes.label: Multi-Architecture Accelerator Build Matrix
nodes.rationale: Frigate ships one image variant per accelerator family (standard amd64/arm64, rpi, tensorrt, tensorrt-jp6, rk, rocm, synaptics) built from per-target bake HCL files, because bundling every runtime into one image would be enormous. The variant suffix list in ci.yml must stay in sync with the retag loop in release.yml.

nodes.label: Stalebot Workflow
nodes.rationale: Daily cron marks issues and PRs stale after 30 days and closes 3 days later, with planned/security/dependencies labels exempt. A commented-out clean_ghcr job for pruning old dev-* container images is retained but disabled.

nodes.label: Pull Request Checks Workflow
nodes.rationale: Python tests, mypy, and the API spec drift check run inside a built devcontainer rather than on the bare runner, so CI executes against the same image contributors develop in. Docs and GitHub template paths are ignored to avoid running the whole matrix on non-code changes. The web unit test step is commented out; only lint, i18n key extraction, build, and Playwright E2E run for the frontend.

nodes.label: Release Workflow (skopeo retagging)
nodes.rationale: Release does not rebuild. It uses skopeo to copy the already-built short-SHA images to version tags, preserving multi-arch manifests, and only applies the :stable tag when the git tag matches a plain vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH pattern so beta tags never become stable.

nodes.label: PR Template Validation Workflow
nodes.rationale: Runs on pull_request_target so it can comment and close on forks. Maintainers and bots (blakeblackshear, NickM-27, hawkeye217, dependabot, weblate) are allowlisted and skipped. Missing sections, an empty Proposed change, or unchecked Type of change / AI disclosure / Checklist boxes cause an explanatory comment plus an automatic close, pushing the compliance cost onto the author rather than the reviewer.

nodes.label: Setup Composite Action (QEMU + Buildx)
nodes.rationale: Stops docker, mounts a maximized virtual volume at /var/lib/docker (about 97G as of 2/14/2024), then restarts docker, because the default GitHub runner disk cannot hold Frigate's multi-stage images. Emits image-name and cache-name outputs derived from the lowercased repo and the 7-char short SHA so every build job tags consistently.

nodes.label: Frigate AI Policy
nodes.rationale: Every discussion template, the feature request template, and the PR template check enforce the same policy: posts or PRs that appear to be AI-generated on a contributor's behalf may be closed without a response. The intent is to keep maintainer triage load bounded by filtering low-signal generated content at intake rather than during review.

nodes.label: Required Diagnostic Bundle
nodes.rationale: All support templates require the same core fields: full version with build identifier, the YAML config, Frigate logs, go2rtc logs, docker-compose or CLI invocation, install method, and object detector. Requiring the bundle up front avoids the multi-round-trip cost of asking each reporter for the same context.

nodes.label: Beta Support Discussion Template
nodes.rationale: Requires config, Frigate logs, install method, compose file, OS and version up front because those are the only things that make a beta report actionable; an AI cannot supply them for the reporter.

nodes.label: Camera Support Discussion Template
nodes.rationale: Additionally requires go2rtc logs and ffprobe output from the camera, since camera/stream issues are almost always diagnosable only from the actual stream parameters.

nodes.label: Frigate Custom Spelling Dictionary
nodes.rationale: Project-specific vocabulary (hardware vendors, camera brands, ML/codec jargon) so the spell checker does not flag domain terms.

nodes.label: Object Detection Model Type
nodes.rationale: Detectors that can run more than one architecture (openvino, onnx, rknn, memryx, axengine, synaptics) need model_type plus matching input_tensor, input_dtype and input_pixel_format because the exported ONNX/DFP file carries no metadata Frigate can trust; a mismatch silently produces garbage detections rather than an error.

nodes.label: 320x320 Default Input Size
nodes.rationale: 320x320 is preferred over 640x640 because Frigate crops video frames to areas of interest before running detection, so the smaller input lowers CPU usage and inference time without measurably hurting accuracy in most scenes.

nodes.label: Memray Binary Crash Recovery

nodes.label: Retention Policy Gate on Segment Storage
nodes.rationale: record.enabled alone keeps nothing: continuous recording is off by default, so cached segments are only moved to disk when they match a configured continuous/motion/alerts/detections retention policy. This conserves storage by default at the cost of being the single most common reason recordings appear empty.

nodes.label: Recording RAM Cache and Maintainer
nodes.rationale: Segments are first written to a RAM cache (/tmp/cache) and moved to disk by frigate.record.maintainer. Frigate discards the oldest cached segments rather than exhausting memory and crashing, trading lost footage for stability.

nodes.label: PIPELINE_ERROR_DECODE Playback Failure
nodes.rationale: Frigate copies the record stream to disk without re-encoding, so the browser must decode exactly what the camera produced. Chromium's media pipeline is stricter than VLC/ffmpeg, so a file valid to ffprobe can still fail in a browser; this is outside Frigate's control by design.

nodes.label: Incompatible Audio Codec in MP4 Container
nodes.rationale: G.711 variants (pcm_alaw/pcm_mulaw) cannot be muxed into MP4, so ffmpeg silently fails to write the segment even while live view works; the fix is transcoding audio to AAC or dropping it via an ffmpeg preset.

nodes.label: Smart Codec / H.264+ Timestamp Corruption
nodes.rationale: Smart/"+" codec modes change encoding parameters mid-stream and drop keyframes, corrupting timestamps so segments split roughly every second and fill the cache 10x faster than expected.

nodes.label: Hourly Preview Clip Assembly

nodes.rationale: Preview frames are cached in tmpfs and only assembled into a clip at the top of each hour, so recreating the container mid-hour discards the partial hour. Expected behavior, unrelated to shm_size; a soft UI restart preserves the cache.
