nodes.label: Face Recognition
nodes.rationale: Runs on the detect-role stream, not recordings, because recording latency would leave notifications without names, embedding models rescale to a fixed input anyway, and motion clarity matters more than extra pixels.

nodes.label: Small and Large Face Embedding Models
nodes.rationale: small runs a FaceNet embedding on CPU for efficiency; large runs ArcFace for accuracy and needs an integrated or discrete GPU/NPU. A landmark model aligns faces first in both cases, and a CPU with AVX + AVX2 is required.

nodes.label: Area-Weighted Multi-Frame Recognition
nodes.source_location: How Frigate Decides Who a Person Is
nodes.rationale: The sub_label comes from all recognition attempts while a person is in view, weighted by face area, so a single very high confidence match cannot assign a label and a few wrong guesses on blurry frames do not change the result.

nodes.label: Face Training Set Construction
nodes.rationale: Diversity matters more than volume: training already-high-scoring, blurry, grayscale/IR or near-duplicate images causes over-fitting and makes unknown people score like known ones. Bulk upload and negative training are deliberately unsupported, and bulk reprocessing is not offered because reprocessing only affects images at a similar angle.

nodes.label: Login Failure Rate Limiting
nodes.rationale: trusted_proxies must list upstream networks, otherwise the rate limit is keyed to the proxy IP and one brute force attempt locks out every other device behind the same proxy.

nodes.label: Upstream Proxy Authentication
nodes.rationale: Frigate deliberately does not implement OIDC, SAML or LDAP natively; as an NVR focused on recording and detection it delegates those protocols to battle-tested proxies and consumes the authenticated user and role through whitelisted headers.

nodes.label: Proxy Role Mapping
nodes.rationale: role_map translates upstream group claims into Frigate roles; admin takes precedence when several mappings match so a user belonging to both admin and viewer groups is not accidentally downgraded.

nodes.label: User Roles and Camera Access
nodes.rationale: Roles are only enforced on the authenticated port 8971; port 5000 treats every request as anonymous with admin-level access by design, for unauthenticated internal use on a trusted network.

nodes.label: Minimum Audio Volume Gate
nodes.rationale: Audio detection only runs above min_volume RMS so the CPU cost mirrors how motion gates object detection; volume above the threshold also counts as motion for recording retention.

nodes.label: Audio Transcription
nodes.rationale: Transcription is user-initiated rather than automatic because it is serialized one event at a time and a queue would need backpressure, prioritization, buffering, retry and crash recovery for little practical value on edge hardware; live transcription is not reused for speech events because the two processes are asynchronous and cannot be aligned reliably.

nodes.label: Hwaccel Presets
nodes.rationale: Beyond shortening the argument list, a hwaccel preset tells Frigate which hardware exists so it can also offload Birdseye restream encoding and stream scaling to the GPU.

nodes.label: Input Args Presets
nodes.rationale: http and rtmp presets cannot be applied to rtsp streams, so when a camera mixes a direct http source with an rtsp restream the preset must be set per stream rather than per camera or ffmpeg crashes.

nodes.label: Hardware Accelerated Video Decoding
nodes.rationale: There is no CPU fallback for hardware acceleration, so a misconfigured preset shows up as ffmpeg errors rather than degraded performance.

nodes.label: Intel GPU Stats via fdinfo
nodes.rationale: Utilization is read from per-client DRM counters in /proc/<pid>/fdinfo, which needs kernel 5.19+ for i915 (any xe release) and permission to read other processes' fdinfo, but avoids intel_gpu_top, CAP_PERFMON, privileged mode and perf_event_paranoid tuning.

nodes.label: Add Camera Wizard
nodes.source_location: Adding a camera with the Add Camera Wizard
nodes.rationale: The wizard probes over ONVIF or templates a brand URL, tests each stream, and writes the go2rtc restream plus live stream mapping so a standard setup needs no hand written YAML; validation catches the common misconfigurations (detect resolution too high or low, non-AAC audio on a record stream, a restreamed input used for record, brand specific stream type mistakes).

nodes.label: Camera Input Roles
nodes.rationale: Each of detect, record and audio may be assigned to only one input per camera, allowing a low resolution stream for detection and a high resolution one for recording. A detect stream is always decoded (for motion, Birdseye and image endpoints) even with object detection disabled, so a low resolution detect role is recommended even for record-only setups.

nodes.label: Camera Deletion Cleanup
nodes.rationale: Deletion removes config, database records and media but deliberately keeps exports so saved footage survives; go2rtc stream entries and camera group references are left behind because they are harmless and outside the camera's own config section. A failed parse restores the previous config rather than leaving Frigate broken.

nodes.label: ONVIF PTZ Controls
nodes.rationale: tls_insecure falls back to plaintext PasswordText for cameras that reject digest tokens, and ignore_time_mismatch compensates for clock skew in ONVIF tokens; both weaken security so NTP on both ends is the preferred fix.

nodes.label: H.265 Apple Compatibility
nodes.rationale: Safari only plays the annexb form of H.265, so apple_compatibility retags the recording stream to keep clips playable on macOS and iPhone.

nodes.label: Reolink Camera Setup
nodes.rationale: http-flv is the most reliable transport for Reolink at 5MP and below; 6MP+ latest generations use http-flv-enhanced over H265 which needs ffmpeg 8.0, older high resolution models need rtsp. Two way talk requires a secondary non-prefixed rtsp stream because go2rtc must own the stream to carry the backchannel.

nodes.label: Birdseye View
nodes.rationale: Each tile is composed from the detect-role stream, so Birdseye image quality follows the detect resolution rather than the recording stream.

nodes.label: PTZ Camera Autotracking
nodes.rationale: Requires ONVIF RelativePanTiltTranslationSpace with a TranslationSpaceFov entry; cameras that only claim support (or never update MoveStatus, as with many Hikvision firmwares) cannot be worked around and autotracking is disabled.

nodes.label: PTZ Calibration and movement_weights
nodes.rationale: Calibration measures PTZ motor speed over a series of moves so Frigate can predict how far to move to recenter an object. The UI and other cameras are intentionally unresponsive during calibration to avoid excessive network and CPU load. Weights keep refining at runtime, so calibrate_on_startup must be turned off afterwards or the refined values are overwritten.

nodes.label: Autotracking Zoom Modes
nodes.rationale: Absolute zoom is conservative and separate from pan/tilt because it works on the widest range of cameras; relative zoom moves concurrently but ONVIF makes no guarantee about how the generic zoom range maps to magnification, so behavior varies by vendor. A high zoom_factor starves the motion estimator of background detail and loses the object.

nodes.label: PTZ Motion Estimator
nodes.rationale: Tracked objects are preserved across camera moves by estimating camera motion from frame detail, which is why a motion mask over the timestamp is recommended and why scenes without hard edges, motion blur, or an over-zoomed object break tracking.

nodes.label: Global and Camera-Level Config Inheritance
nodes.rationale: A camera value counts as an override because it is written in the config, not because it differs from the global value, so repeating the global value still detaches the camera; the key must be deleted to inherit again. Overrides apply per value, not per section.

nodes.label: Lists Replace, Maps Merge
nodes.rationale: A camera list takes the place of the global list rather than adding to it, which makes an empty list the normal way to opt a camera out; maps merge key by key so a camera can add one filter without redeclaring the inherited ones.

nodes.label: Globally Gated Enrichments
nodes.source_location: Enrichments that must be enabled globally first
nodes.rationale: lpr and face_recognition must be enabled globally before any camera can use them because the global setting controls whether the supporting background process starts at all; enabling one only on a camera is a startup error. Audio transcription does not work this way.

nodes.label: Hardware Accelerated Enrichments
nodes.rationale: Enrichment acceleration is independent of object detection acceleration and is selected by choosing the matching Frigate image (-rocm, -tensorrt, -tensorrt-jp6, -rk, default for OpenVINO). ROCm disables unstable models on purpose. A Coral is a TPU and accelerates nothing here. tensorrt for detection plus Intel iGPU for enrichments is unsupported.

nodes.label: go2rtc Integration
nodes.rationale: go2rtc powers WebRTC/MSE live view with audio and higher resolution than jsmpeg, Home Assistant live streams, and an RTSP relay that reduces the number of connections to each camera. Naming the go2rtc stream after the camera lets Frigate auto-map it to better live view options.

nodes.label: Full Reference Config
nodes.rationale: Documented as a reference only, not a template: copying it wholesale pins defaults that may change between versions, so only values differing from defaults should be specified.

nodes.label: Motion Detection Configuration
nodes.rationale: Motion is the gate for object detection so it cannot be disabled while detect is enabled; lightning_threshold exists so scene-wide changes (lightning, IR switch, PTZ move) recalibrate instead of flooding the tracker.

nodes.label: Recording Retention Modes
nodes.rationale: Alert/detection retain modes cannot recover segments a more restrictive camera-level retain mode already discarded, so the camera-level mode must be the least restrictive of the two.

nodes.label: Named Config Profiles
nodes.rationale: Profiles are partial camera overrides toggled at runtime and applied on top of the already-resolved config, so they win over camera and global values without rewriting the config file.

nodes.label: environment_vars Substitution
nodes.rationale: Provided for Home Assistant OS users who cannot set container environment variables; values are stored in plain text in the config, so Docker env vars or secrets remain the recommended way to keep credentials out of the config. go2rtc is excluded because it is a separate process that only sees the container environment.

nodes.label: Labelmap Customization
nodes.rationale: Labels can be renamed but not added, because the mapping only relabels existing model classes. Renaming breaks alert labels, objects.track lists, and the special person/face and car/license_plate attribute associations, so those must be updated together.

nodes.label: Internal and External Listen Ports
nodes.rationale: Internal (5000) and external (8971) ports must differ and Frigate refuses to start otherwise, because requests on the internal port are treated as authenticated admins; sharing a port would strip authentication from the external one. Nginx binds at startup so changes need a restart.

nodes.label: Config Validation Workflow
nodes.rationale: Frigate exits on an invalid config at startup, so validation is offered through the WebUI, the /api/config/save endpoint (returns 400 on invalid), and a --validate-config container run that returns 1/0 for CI use, to avoid a failed restart taking the NVR offline.

nodes.label: Normalized Camera Crop Region
nodes.rationale: Crop coordinates are fractions of the camera's detect width/height rather than pixels so a crop stays valid independent of detect resolution; a tight crop avoids extra signals unrelated to the state.

nodes.label: Consecutive State Verification
nodes.rationale: A pending state change requires 3 consecutive identical classifications before it is published, preventing the published state from flipping on a single noisy frame.

nodes.label: Recent Classifications Save Policy
nodes.rationale: Images are only stored on first detection, state changes, pending verification, or sub-100% scores; stable 100% matches are skipped to avoid storing redundant high-confidence classifications.

nodes.label: State Model Diversity Over Volume
nodes.rationale: Homogeneous training data yields models that work under the original conditions but destabilize when day turns to night or seasons shift, which is why bulk training is not offered in the UI.

nodes.label: Sub Label Classification Type
nodes.rationale: A tracked object can hold only one sub label, so face recognition, LPR, triggers and a sub_label classification model race each other; the attribute type is recommended when collisions are possible.

nodes.label: Attribute Classification Type
nodes.rationale: Attributes are metadata that can coexist independently on one object, so multiple simultaneous properties (helmet, vest, backpack) can be represented without contention.

nodes.label: Threshold and Class Consensus Assignment
nodes.rationale: Requiring both a per-attempt threshold (default 0.8) and 60% agreement across at least 3 attempts prevents false positives from a single lucky frame before a sub label or attribute is committed.

nodes.label: The none Class
nodes.source_location: none works differently from named classes
nodes.rationale: Named classes want visually uniform examples, but none must absorb everything unknown at inference, so it needs deliberate visual diversity (small crops, partial views, false positives) or the model forces ambiguous crops into a named class.

nodes.label: Diversity Over Volume Training Principle
nodes.rationale: MobileNetV2 overfits quickly on homogeneous data and learns a single moment rather than the class, which is the stated reason Frigate deliberately does not implement bulk training in the UI.

nodes.label: Minimum Crop Size Guidance
nodes.rationale: Crops under ~80x80 are stretched 3-7x by the 224x224 model input resize and collapse into a generic blob region of feature space, so aim for at least 100x100 or reposition the camera.

nodes.label: Class Balance Rule
nodes.rationale: Keeping the largest class within ~3x the smallest avoids bias where borderline predictions default to the dominant class (the 'everything looks like Buddy' failure mode).

nodes.label: Structured Review Summary Schema
nodes.source_location: Review Summary Usage and Best Practices
nodes.rationale: The JSON schema (title, scene, shortSummary, confidence, other_concerns, potential_threat_level) lets notifications show a short form while the UI keeps the full narrative; smaller models often fail to follow it, producing parse errors.

nodes.label: Activity Context Prompt
nodes.rationale: Normal activity differs per installation and per camera, so the prompt is overridable globally and per camera, but must not be overly specific because it sways the model's threat level scoring.

nodes.label: Potential Threat Level Scale
nodes.rationale: Levels 0/1/2 are evaluated in order (verified person, then time and action checks, then escalation on weapons or forced entry) so that an unidentified person in private areas at night is always flagged for human review.

nodes.label: Review Image Source Selection
nodes.rationale: Preview frames use fewer tokens per image while recordings give 480p detail for plates and text; recordings cost more tokens so fewer frames fit, and the system falls back to previews when recordings are unavailable.

nodes.label: Dynamic Frame Count Budgeting
nodes.rationale: Frame counts are computed from context window size, camera aspect ratio and image source to fill ~98% of the context while capping at 20 frames to keep inference times reasonable.

nodes.label: Review Reports
nodes.rationale: Aggregates suspicious review items across cameras over a time window into one report, requestable via the summarize API or the frigate.review_summarize Home Assistant service for vacation or daily digests.

nodes.label: Intent-Focused Prompting
nodes.rationale: Default prompts ask for intent rather than appearance because descriptions say what is happening while intent gives context, letting loitering or after-hours approach trigger attention sooner than a neutral appearance caption.

nodes.label: Layered Custom Prompts
nodes.rationale: Prompts resolve global then camera then per-object-label, with only {label}, {sub_label} and {camera} substituted, so a per-label prompt can be tuned without losing the global default.

nodes.label: Snapshot vs Thumbnail Source
nodes.rationale: use_snapshot trades multi-frame movement and direction cues for a single higher quality image, which is useful when regenerating a description but limits the model's ability to judge motion.

nodes.label: Description Send Triggers
nodes.rationale: Requests fire at the end of the tracked object lifecycle by default, or earlier after a number of significantly changed frames for more real-time notifications.

nodes.label: GenAI Provider Roles
nodes.rationale: genai is a map of named providers where each role (chat, descriptions, embeddings) is assigned to exactly one provider, so roles can be split across specialized backends or served by a single provider.

nodes.label: Embeddings Role Model Requirement
nodes.rationale: Text queries are matched against stored image embeddings, so the model must place images and text in the same vector space; a chat or description model still returns vectors but retrieval quality silently degrades with no error.

nodes.label: Provider Context Size Override
nodes.rationale: Frigate derives the number of frames to send from the context size the provider reports; when a server misreports or does not expose it, provider_options.context_size pins the value so frames are not truncated and requests do not fail.

nodes.label: Instruct vs Thinking Model Modes
nodes.rationale: Description tasks are synthesis-only and benefit from concise output, so Frigate disables thinking for those calls when the model exposes a per-request toggle; chat leaves the toggle to the user.

nodes.label: GenAI Request Debug Artifacts
nodes.source_location: FAQ: How do I debug GenAI issues?
nodes.rationale: debug_save_thumbnails writes the exact frames, prompt.txt and response.txt to /media/frigate/clips/genai-requests/ so poor results can be attributed to the image or the prompt before blaming the model.

nodes.label: GenAI Debugging Workflow
nodes.rationale: Provider configuration, object descriptions and review descriptions are enabled independently; a descriptions provider is only contacted on first use, so a working config can look broken until the feature itself is enabled.

nodes.rationale: SBC-specific acceleration frameworks are too varied and low-userbase for core maintainers to support, so a community codeowner supplies the code, maintenance and user support for each board.

nodes.label: Board Bake File (board.hcl)
nodes.rationale: Lets the community board image build against the main build as cache, giving a clean base and faster builds; board builds pull from cache but never push to it.

nodes.label: Board Dockerfile Contract
nodes.rationale: All board-specific work must start FROM deps and copy rootfs from the main Frigate build so board images stay layered on the shared base.

nodes.label: Detect, Record and Stream Roles
nodes.rationale: Only the detect stream is decoded for processing, so tuning resolution and fps at the camera avoids wasting CPU decoding frames Frigate immediately discards; matching aspect ratios across streams keeps live and playback seamless.

nodes.label: Choosing a Detect Resolution
nodes.rationale: Frigate crops a motion region and resizes it to the model's 320x320 input, so extra resolution is lost in the resize and only helps when objects are very small in the frame.

nodes.label: Choosing a Detect Frame Rate
nodes.rationale: Tracking matches bounding boxes between detection frames, and 5 fps already yields ~15 detections for an object visible several seconds; raising it scales detection load linearly with no tracking benefit unless an object crosses the whole frame in under two seconds, where camera placement is the real fix.

nodes.label: Frigate Introduction
nodes.rationale: Design goals: minimize resource use by only looking for objects when and where necessary, lean on multiprocessing, and prioritize realtime over processing every frame.

nodes.label: Object Detection Accelerator (Detector)
nodes.rationale: Frigate is designed around very low inference times; offloading TensorFlow to a detector is an order of magnitude faster and dramatically reduces CPU load, so the CPU only screens for motion and hands regions to the accelerator.

nodes.label: Google Coral EdgeTPU
nodes.rationale: No longer recommended for new installs except in low-power deployments, but still supported because it remains one of the most power-efficient devices for running detection models.

nodes.label: MemryX MX3
nodes.rationale: Being a pipelined architecture, its camera capacity cannot be derived from 1/latency, so the separately measured MX3 Total FPS column is the correct sizing metric.

nodes.label: Apple Silicon Detector
nodes.rationale: Apple Silicon cannot run inside a container, so a ZMQ proxy bridges to a host-side detector process, adding minimal latency only when run on the same device.

nodes.label: CPU Motion Screening vs Detector Inference
nodes.source_location: What does Frigate use the CPU for
nodes.rationale: The CPU watches for movement and only forwards those frames to the detector, keeping one accelerator available to many cameras; raising resolution or frame rate increases work for both the decoder and the detector.

nodes.label: Planning a New Installation
nodes.rationale: Hardware sizing is driven by simultaneous activity rather than raw camera count, because detection load only occurs when motion regions are actually being submitted.

nodes.label: Storage Planning (SSD vs HDD vs NAS)
nodes.rationale: Modern SSD wear-leveling and TBW ratings make the old wear-out concern obsolete, HDDs still win on cost per gigabyte for long retention, and NAS adds latency and network dependency so local storage is preferred.

nodes.label: RAM Sizing Tiers
nodes.rationale: 4GB covers a basic setup, 8GB is the floor once enrichment models must be loaded, and 16GB is recommended for many cameras or heavy enrichment use to avoid swapping.

nodes.label: Container Storage Paths
nodes.rationale: /config holds config and the SQLite DB, /media/frigate holds clips, recordings and exports, and /tmp/cache should be tmpfs because segments are written there before conversion to mp4.

nodes.label: shm-size Calculation
nodes.rationale: Decoded frames live in shared memory, so undersized /dev/shm produces 'Bus error' exits; logs also consume up to 40MB of shm and must be included in the math.

nodes.label: Process and File Descriptor Limits
nodes.rationale: Hitting the PID limit logs 'can't start new thread' followed by a Bus error that mimics an shm sizing problem, so pids-limit and nofile ulimits must be checked before enlarging shm further.

nodes.label: Frigate Network Ports
nodes.rationale: 8971 is the authenticated UI/API entry point for reverse proxies while 5000 is unauthenticated and should be restricted to the docker network; 8554 restreams RTSP and 8555 carries WebRTC.

nodes.label: Home Assistant App Installation
nodes.rationale: The App is not the Home Assistant integration; HA OS lacks the mesa driver, NPU firmware and Nvidia runtime, so those accelerators are unavailable and hardware acceleration may require the Full Access variant.

nodes.label: Virtualization Guidance (Proxmox / ESXi)
nodes.rationale: Frigate wants low overhead access to Coral and GPU devices, so bare metal Debian is preferred; if virtualized, a QEMU VM with ballooning disabled is recommended over LXC because passing devices through two container layers is difficult and unsupported.

nodes.label: One-Time Model Downloads and model_cache
nodes.rationale: Models download on first enablement and are cached in /config/model_cache/, so later startups need no internet; MobileNetV2 training base weights are the exception, fetched only when a training run starts and cached outside /config unless redirected.

nodes.label: Model Download Mirror Environment Variables
nodes.rationale: HF_ENDPOINT, GITHUB_ENDPOINT, GITHUB_RAW_ENDPOINT and TF_KERAS_MOBILENET_V2_WEIGHTS_URL let restricted installs point downloads at internal mirrors instead of the public hosts.

nodes.label: Running Frigate Offline
nodes.rationale: Air-gapped operation requires pre-caching models, pre-fetching training base weights, disabling the version check and setting HF_HUB_OFFLINE/TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE; TF_KERAS_MOBILENET_V2_WEIGHTS_URL must be set even when never contacted or Frigate ignores the manually copied weights.

nodes.label: Motion Mask
nodes.rationale: Stops motion in the masked area from triggering object detection but does not suppress detection of objects there when a nearby area triggers, so it suits constantly changing regions that never hold objects of interest.

nodes.label: Object Filter Mask
nodes.rationale: Drops any bounding box whose bottom center falls inside the mask, forcing it to be treated as a false positive; overlap elsewhere in the box does not matter.

nodes.label: Updating Frigate
nodes.rationale: Back up /config including frigate.db before updating so a rollback can restore both the config and the database alongside an older image tag.

nodes.label: Semantic Search Usage Practices
nodes.source_location: Semantic Search - Usage and best practices
nodes.rationale: Because of how the embedding models are trained, description matches outrank thumbnail matches in multi-modal search even when the thumbnail embedding is closer; thumbnail queries should be phrased as image captions and work best on large subjects.

nodes.label: Export (Retention-Exempt Footage Copy)
nodes.rationale: Exports are stored separately under /media/frigate/exports and are never removed by retention, so a single important clip can be preserved without raising retention for an entire camera; the tradeoff is that exports accumulate until manually deleted.

nodes.label: Smart Streaming
nodes.rationale: A camera's image refreshes about once per minute while idle and switches to a full live stream only when activity is detected, conserving bandwidth and CPU on multi-camera dashboards.

nodes.label: Camera Group Dashboard
nodes.rationale: Group layouts and per-camera streaming settings are stored per browser/device rather than in the config file, so each device can keep its own arrangement.

nodes.label: Review Item (Alerts, Detections, Motion)
nodes.rationale: Not all captured video is equally interesting, so activity on one camera is bundled into review items and sorted by importance into alerts, detections, and motion; reviewed state is per user so triage by one person does not hide items from others.

nodes.label: Motion Search
nodes.rationale: Re-analyzes saved recordings on demand instead of reading a pre-built index, so it can recover changes the live motion detector missed (masked regions, lightning_threshold pauses, undetected objects). Segments with no recorded motion in the ROI are skipped using the stored motion heatmap, which is what makes long ranges practical.

nodes.label: Annotation Offset
nodes.rationale: A fine timing correction that realigns bounding-box overlays with recorded video when the camera's snapshot and recording timestamps drift; admins can persist it to the camera config.

nodes.label: Per-endpoint access annotation (x-required-role)
nodes.rationale: Every generated operation carries an x-required-role marker (public / any / camera / admin) and an Access line prefixed to its description, so the auth requirement of each endpoint is documented rather than implied. The file is machine generated by generate_api_auth_spec.py and never hand edited; info.title is deliberately empty because docusaurus-openapi-docs treats that as the signal to suppress the generated API introduction page.

nodes.label: Frigate brand asset trademark notice
nodes.rationale: Logos and icons are carved out of the repository's MIT license and held as common law trademarks of Frigate, Inc. Nominative use and running the local UI are permitted, but forks that distribute a modified or competing build must swap in their own assets so the marks cannot signal endorsement or official status.
